summary: Built hubreg, a home-automation action registry where each device action is one validated record that drives the assistant's tool schemas, the app's controls, the hub's argument checking, the refusals, help and a walk over the catalogue. The package has a registry, binder, diagnoser, describer and walker, four demo plug-ins (thermostat, light, door, scene), and a CLI (describe / call, plus help and walk helpers). Every consumer reads the same records, registration refuses malformed or inconsistent records, and 169 standard-library tests pass with python3 -m unittest discover -s tests.

pattern_mapping.Operation record: hubreg/record.py::Record (built and validated by build_record); one per (on, name) with args, fields, samples, run, flags, redirects, validate, doc
pattern_mapping.Argument spec: hubreg/record.py::Spec — name, type, unit, doc, default/optional, min/max, usual + usual_hint, enum values, option redirects
pattern_mapping.Flags: record['flags'] = {'confirm': bool} plus Registry.needs_confirmation, where the host's confirm_required set and the record flag are OR-ed so a plug-in cannot lower the requirement (hubreg/registry.py)
pattern_mapping.Registry: hubreg/registry.py::Registry — register (validates), finalize (cross-record redirect checks), lookup/get/names/kinds/records, and every consumer entry point
pattern_mapping.Binder: hubreg/binding.py::bind_record -> Call(record_name, on, args, warnings) or Failure; order: unknown options, then per-spec supplied/default/optional/missing, type, hard limits, usual-range warning, cross-argument hook
pattern_mapping.Describer: hubreg/describe.py — context_line (short form), help_text (full), controls (one per argument for the app), tool_schema (assistant), all rendered from the same specs
pattern_mapping.Diagnoser: hubreg/diagnose.py::explain — turns a Failure into a Refusal with valid names, nearest name, redirect-beats-nearest fix, enum nearest value, clamped range fix; confirm_refusal builds E_CONFIRM
pattern_mapping.Walker: hubreg/walker.py::walk, exposed as Registry.walk() — renders help/schema/controls, checks redirects, binds and runs every sample with confirmed=True, compares result keys with the declared fields
pattern_mapping.Argument types (pluggable): hubreg/argtypes.py — number/string/bool/enum objects with accepts/json_schema/render, plus register_type so a domain adds a type without touching core or consumers
pattern_mapping.Module registration: hubreg/demo.py::demo_registry — the four demo plug-in records registered and finalised at start-up; hubreg/__main__.py + hubreg/cli.py are the command line
pattern_mapping.Exceptions outside the registry: hubreg/cli.py's argument parsing (key=value, --confirm) is the only hand-written part; it holds no action list and always goes through Registry.bind/run

notes_applied: Note 1 (validate structure and consistency): register refuses unknown/missing keys, non-callable run, duplicate fields, duplicate argument names, required-after-optional, untyped arguments, defaults outside limits or of the wrong type, usual ranges outside limits or without a hint, option redirects to no argument or onto themselves, limits/usual on a non-number, and samples that do not bind; cross-record action redirects are checked in Registry.finalize at the end of start-up.

Note 2 (hard limits vs usual ranges, unknown keys first): outside min/max is E_ARG_RANGE with a clamped fix, outside usual binds with a RANGE warning that carries the hint, defaults never warn, and unknown options are reported before missing arguments so 'temp' gets 'renamed: use target'.

Note 3 (nothing falls back silently): unknown keys and wrong types are refusals, no coercion (bool is rejected where a number is expected), and plug-in results are checked against the declared fields (ResultError, not a silent pass).

Note 4 (redirects live in the records): option redirects are argSpec['redirects'] and action redirects are record['redirects'], so the diagnoser, help and walker all see them; test_agreement scans the core and consumers to prove no second name table exists.

Note 5 (walk the registry, know its limits; samples in the record): every record carries 'samples' which registration requires and validates, Registry.walk() exercises each sample and reports action/phase/problem, and the tests add separate limit, redirect, warning and optional-argument cases.

Note 6 (pluggable types, consumers outside the core): hubreg/argtypes.py holds accept/json_schema/render per type with register_type; tests/test_argtypes.py adds a 'colour' type from outside the core and the binder, tool schema, controls, help and walk all handle it unchanged.
Note 7 (one record per receiver kind and name): records are keyed by (on, name); a duplicate is E_DUPLICATE and the same name on another device kind is a separate action.
Note 9 (enumerate exceptions): the only non-record part is the CLI's argv parsing, it holds no action knowledge, and test_agreement.py asserts that the core and consumer modules never name an action.

Note 2/Flags (confirmation): the host's confirm_required decides, the record flag can only add, run() raises E_CONFIRM whose fix is the same call with confirmed=true, and the CLI refuses a security action non-interactively unless --confirm is passed.
tests: 169 unittest tests across 10 files (interface, records, bind, run, consumers, walk, demo, cli, argtypes, agreement); last run: `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` -> Ran 169 tests in 0.481s, OK.
chapter_feedback: The structure table and Sketch mapped almost one-to-one onto TASK.md, which made the design quick; the binder/diagnoser split (Failure internal, Refusal public) was the single most useful thing to copy.

The chapter's record has fields(boundArgs) and an 'expand' alternative to 'run'; TASK.md has a flat fields list and implementation only, so note 10 and the 'expanded operations' idea had no home here — a note on how to degrade gracefully would help.

Note 2 names usual ranges and hints, but TASK.md's ArgSpec list omits them while requiring RANGE warnings; I added 'usual'/'usual_hint' as extra optional keys, which is a guess about how far the task's schema can be extended.

The chapter never says where a rename redirect is stored: my first Registry.finalize refused a record whose redirect target was itself, which broke every normal rename ('set_temp' -> 'set_temperature' on the new record). A sentence saying the *new* record carries the old name would save that mistake.

The diagnoser sketch gives the fix only from a registered redirect; for a plain typo ('pign' for 'ping') the chapter's refusal would carry no fix at all. I added a similarity threshold (0.7, documented) to offer the nearest name, and the chapter could say whether that is intended.

Note 1 says goja-cv does not check defaults against limits and calls it a mistake, but gives no guidance on the edges: I had to decide that 'default' and 'optional' are alternatives, that a None default is invalid, and that limits on a string argument are refused.

Note 5's warning that the walker proves little was accurate and useful: the walk passes on one call per sample, so most of my real coverage had to be written by hand (tests/test_bind.py, test_run.py).

The chapter's 'confirm' flag discussion (host decides, plug-in cannot lower) was clear and translated directly into Registry.needs_confirmation accepting either 'lock_door' or 'door.lock_door', a form the task leaves open.

'Any other list of operations found outside the registry is a bug' is a strong claim to implement; I turned it into a test that scans the core and consumer modules for action names, which is crude but catches a second table.
